creative.hook: Travel through ten animal habitats and finish with a three-heart boss question.
creative.learningGoal: Recognize animal traits and connect them to habitat, movement, and classification.
creative.signatureMoment: The final octopus question becomes the expedition boss challenge.

researchSources.title: Smithsonian's National Zoo animal fact sheets
San Diego Zoo Wildlife Explorers animal facts

questions.question: Which animal says meow?
questions.explanation: Cats meow to communicate with people and other cats.

questions.question: Which animal has a very long neck?
questions.explanation: A giraffe's long neck helps it reach leaves high in trees.

questions.question: True or false: Penguins can fly.
questions.explanation: Penguins cannot fly, but they are excellent swimmers.

questions.question: Which is the fastest land animal?
questions.explanation: A cheetah's flexible body and long tail help it sprint and turn.

questions.question: Who am I?
questions.explanation: Elephants use their trunks to smell, drink, and pick things up.

questions.question: Which animal is a mammal?
questions.explanation: Dolphins breathe air and feed milk to their babies.

questions.question: Which striped animal lives in Asia?
questions.explanation: Wild tigers live in parts of Asia, and each has a unique stripe pattern.

questions.question: True or false: A bat is a bird.
questions.explanation: A bat is a mammal and the only mammal capable of true flight.

questions.question: Who am I?
questions.explanation: The platypus is one of the few mammals that lays eggs.

questions.question: Which animal has three hearts?
questions.explanation: An octopus has three hearts: one for its body and two for its gills.
